use_case: Software delivery portfolio tracking, sprint execution, and blocker/risk management across utility technology programs
space_title: Meridian Grid - Software Delivery Project Management 🗂️
space_description:
**Scenario:** You run software delivery at Meridian Grid, where the Grid Modernization and AMI Rollout programs are both mid-sprint and the PUC-facing commitments don't move. Blockers are piling up on a handful of epics, tickets are aging in review, and your next steering readout is tomorrow. Where do you focus to protect the sprint?

**Questions:**

1. Showcase the different visualization options with interesting aspects of the dataset (agent)
2. What are the open blockers flagged High risk by project and epic, and how many days has each been stuck in its current status? (agent)
3. Which epics have the most high-risk blockers and the longest average time-in-status, and how does that compare to their sprint velocity? (agent)

tables.description: Individual work-log entries by engineer across JIRA issues, capturing hours logged, issue type, team, and resolution status.

columns.name: worklog_id
columns.comment: Unique worklog entry identifier

columns.name: work_date
columns.comment: Date the work was logged

columns.name: issue_key
columns.comment: JIRA issue key (e.g. GRID-1001, AMI-2012)

columns.name: project
columns.comment: Project name: Grid Modernization, AMI Rollout, Outage Management System, DERMS, Customer Portal, SCADA Upgrade, EV Charging Network

columns.name: epic
columns.comment: Epic grouping issues within the project (e.g. Smart Grid Infrastructure, Meter Deployment Pipeline)

columns.name: assignee
columns.comment: Full name of engineer who logged the work (e.g. Bob Chen, Priya Nair, Lena Kowalski)

columns.name: issue_type
columns.comment: JIRA issue type: Story, Bug, Task, Feature, Sub-task, Epic
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {status_noise} < 0.42 THEN 'Story' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.60 THEN 'Bug' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.74 THEN 'Task' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.86 THEN 'Feature' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.94 THEN 'Sub-task' ELSE 'Epic' END

columns.name: team
columns.comment: Engineering team: Platform, Data, Field Systems, Customer Apps, SRE
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.24 THEN 'Platform' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.44 THEN 'Data' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.62 THEN 'Field Systems' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.82 THEN 'Customer Apps' ELSE 'SRE' END

columns.name: hours_logged
columns.comment: Hours logged on the issue for this entry (0.5–8.0 hrs)

columns.name: status_at_log
columns.comment: Issue status at the time of the worklog: In Progress, In Review, To Do, Done, Blocked
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.30 THEN 'In Progress' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.55 THEN 'In Review' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.75 THEN 'To Do' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.90 THEN 'Done' ELSE 'Blocked' END

columns.name: is_resolved
columns.comment: 1 if the issue was resolved at time of log, 0 otherwise
columns.generation_expr: CAST(CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.18 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS INT)

tables.description: Daily snapshot of JIRA issue status, priority, risk level, and age-in-status for open issues across all programs.

columns.name: snapshot_id
columns.comment: Unique snapshot record identifier
columns.generation_expr: CONCAT('IS-', LPAD(CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY d.dt, e.issue_key) AS STRING), 7, '0'))

columns.name: snapshot_date
columns.comment: Date this snapshot was taken

columns.name: issue_key
columns.comment: JIRA issue key (e.g. GRID-1001, AMI-2012, OMS-3018)

columns.name: project
columns.comment: Project name: Grid Modernization, AMI Rollout, Outage Management System, DERMS, Customer Portal, SCADA Upgrade, EV Charging Network

columns.name: epic
columns.comment: Epic grouping issues within the project

columns.name: sprint
columns.comment: Active sprint for the issue (e.g. GRID Sprint 24, AMI Sprint 18)

columns.name: assignee
columns.comment: Full name of engineer assigned to the issue (e.g. Bob Chen, Priya Nair)

columns.name: status
columns.comment: Issue status: Backlog, To Do, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {status_noise} < 0.20 THEN 'Backlog' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.36 THEN 'To Do' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.60 THEN 'In Progress' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.74 THEN 'In Review' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.86 THEN 'Blocked' ELSE 'Done' END

columns.name: priority
columns.comment: Issue priority: Highest, High, Medium, Low
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.12 THEN 'Highest' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.38 THEN 'High' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.75 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END

columns.name: risk_level
columns.comment: Risk level: High, Medium, Low
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.22 THEN 'High' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.55 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END

columns.name: is_blocker
columns.comment: 1 if this issue is flagged as a blocker, 0 otherwise
columns.generation_expr: CAST(CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS INT)

columns.name: days_in_status
columns.comment: Number of days the issue has been in its current status

columns.name: story_points
columns.comment: Story points estimated for the issue (Fibonacci: 1,2,3,5,8,13)
columns.generation_expr: CAST(ELEMENT_AT(ARRAY(1,2,3,5,8,13), 1 + CAST(FLOOR({qty_noise2} * 6) AS INT)) AS INT)

columns.name: project

measures.name: max_days_in_status
measures.comment: Maximum days any issue has been in its current status

genie_instructions:
DOMAIN CONTEXT
This space supports software delivery portfolio tracking and sprint execution for Meridian Grid's utility technology programs. Stakeholders include delivery leads, scrum masters, and program managers. The portfolio spans 7 programs: Grid Modernization (GRID), AMI Rollout (AMI), Outage Management System (OMS), DERMS, Customer Portal (PORTAL), SCADA Upgrade (SCADA), and EV Charging Network (EVSE). Issues are managed in JIRA; worklogs capture engineer time; snapshots track daily issue state; velocity table rolls up monthly sprint performance.

METRIC DEFINITIONS
- velocity = completed_points / committed_points (as a percentage in sprint_velocity_monthly)
- blocker = is_blocker = 1 in jira_issue_snapshots
- high-risk blocker = is_blocker = 1 AND risk_level = 'High' in jira_issue_snapshots
- cycle time = avg_cycle_time_days in sprint_velocity_monthly (issue start to done)
- 'stuck' = high days_in_status in jira_issue_snapshots (issues with days_in_status > 14 are considered stuck)
- story hours = hours logged on issues where issue_type = 'Story'

QUERY GUIDANCE
- ALWAYS prefer metric views with MEASURE() syntax for aggregations.
  - jira_worklogs_metrics (source: jira_worklogs) — dims: work_date, project, epic, issue_type, assignee, team; measures: worklog_count, total_hours_logged, story_hours, resolved_issue_count, distinct_issue_count, distinct_assignee_count.
  - jira_issue_snapshots_metrics (source: jira_issue_snapshots) — dims: snapshot_date, project, epic, sprint, assignee, status, priority, risk_level; measures: open_issue_count, blocker_count, high_risk_blocker_count, avg_days_in_status, max_days_in_status, total_story_points.
- Use GROUP BY ALL with MEASURE() queries.
- For monthly trends, always wrap the date in DATE_TRUNC('month', <date_col>).
- For 'Top X' requests, return LIMIT 10 unless the user specifies otherwise.
- Query base tables directly when needing columns not in metric views (e.g. days_in_status, story_points, sprint_velocity_monthly columns).
- Assignees are stored as full names; map a bare first name to the full name (e.g. 'Bob' -> 'Bob Chen', 'Priya' -> 'Priya Nair').
- When the user's phrasing matches a SQL snippet display name (filters, expressions, or measures), prefer that snippet.
sample_questions: Showcase the different visualization options with interesting aspects of the dataset
What are the open blockers flagged High risk by project and epic, and how many days has each been stuck in its current status?
Which epics have the most high-risk blockers and the longest average time-in-status, and how does that compare to their sprint velocity?

example_sqls.question: What is the monthly trend in total hours logged?
sql_lines: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', work_date) AS month, MEASURE(total_hours_logged) AS total_hours_logged

example_sqls.question: How many high-risk blockers are there by project?
What is the total hours logged by team?
What is the average time issues spend in their current status by project?
How many hours has each engineer logged on Story issues?
Which open blockers have been stuck in their current status the longest?
sql_lines: SELECT issue_key, project, epic, assignee, status, days_in_status

example_sqls.question: What is the average sprint velocity and cycle time by project?
sql_lines: SELECT project, AVG(velocity) AS avg_velocity_pct, AVG(avg_cycle_time_days) AS avg_cycle_time_days

filters.instruction: Use when filtering for high-risk blocker issues in jira_issue_snapshots.
Use when filtering worklogs to Story issue type only.
Use when identifying issues that have been in their current status for more than 14 days.

expressions.sql: CASE WHEN sprint_velocity_monthly.avg_cycle_time_days <= 5 THEN 'Fast (<= 5d)' WHEN sprint_velocity_monthly.avg_cycle_time_days <= 10 THEN 'Normal (6-10d)' WHEN sprint_velocity_monthly.avg_cycle_time_days <= 15 THEN 'Slow (11-15d)' ELSE 'Very Slow (>15d)' END

measures.instruction: Use to aggregate total hours logged from jira_worklogs.

measures.sql: SUM(CASE WHEN jira_issue_snapshots.is_blocker = 1 AND jira_issue_snapshots.risk_level = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
measures.instruction: Counts blockers where risk_level is High from jira_issue_snapshots.
Average number of days issues have been in their current status.
Total features deployed to production from sprint_velocity_monthly.

benchmarks.question: What is the monthly trend in features deployed?
sql_lines: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', report_month) AS month, SUM(features_deployed) AS total_features_deployed

benchmarks.question: How many high-risk blockers are open by project and epic?
sql_lines: SELECT project, epic, MEASURE(high_risk_blocker_count) AS high_risk_blocker_count

benchmarks.question: What are the Top 10 issues with the most days stuck in their current status?
sql_lines: SELECT issue_key, project, epic, assignee, status, days_in_status

benchmarks.question: How many features were deployed in the last quarter by project?
What are the committed versus completed story points for each sprint?
sql_lines: SELECT project, sprint, SUM(committed_points) AS committed_points, SUM(completed_points) AS completed_points

benchmarks.question: How many hours has Bob Chen logged on Story issues in the last 14 days?
sql_lines: WHERE assignee = 'Bob Chen' AND work_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), 14)

benchmarks.question: What is the status breakdown of issues for the Grid Modernization project?
sql_lines: SELECT status, COUNT(DISTINCT issue_key) AS issue_count
